constants.name: Speed of light in vacuum
constants.description: How fast light and all electromagnetic waves travel in a vacuum. Since 1983 the metre is defined from it, so the value is exact.

constants.name: Planck constant
constants.description: Links the energy of a photon to its frequency (E = h f). It sets the scale of quantum effects and has defined the kilogram since 2019.

constants.name: Reduced Planck constant
constants.description: The Planck constant divided by 2π, written ħ (h-bar). It appears naturally when angular frequency is used instead of frequency. Exact, shown to 10 significant figures.
constants.source: Derived from the SI defining constant h (CODATA 2018)

constants.name: Elementary charge
constants.description: The size of the charge on one proton (and minus the charge on one electron). Numerically it is also the number of joules in one electronvolt.

constants.name: Boltzmann constant
constants.description: Converts temperature into energy per particle: a typical molecular energy is of order k_B T. It has defined the kelvin since 2019.

constants.name: Avogadro constant
constants.description: The number of particles in one mole of anything. It connects the atomic scale to amounts you can weigh in the lab.

constants.name: Molar gas constant
constants.description: The Boltzmann constant multiplied by the Avogadro constant: energy per mole per kelvin. It appears in the ideal gas law pV = nRT and in chemical thermodynamics.

constants.name: Faraday constant
constants.description: The electric charge carried by one mole of electrons (N_A times the elementary charge). Used in electrolysis and electrochemistry.

constants.name: Stefan-Boltzmann constant
constants.description: Sets how much power a perfect black body radiates per square metre at a given temperature (P/A = σT⁴). Exact, shown to 10 significant figures.

constants.name: Wien wavelength displacement constant
constants.description: The peak wavelength of black body radiation times the temperature. Hotter bodies glow at shorter wavelengths. Exact, shown to 10 significant figures.

constants.name: Newtonian constant of gravitation
constants.description: Sets the strength of gravity in Newton's law F = G m₁ m₂ / r². It is the least precisely known fundamental constant because gravity is so weak.

constants.name: Standard acceleration of gravity
constants.description: A conventional value of free-fall acceleration near Earth's surface, used to define units such as the kilogram-force. The real value varies from about 9.78 to 9.83 m/s² with latitude and height.

constants.name: Electron mass
constants.description: The rest mass of an electron, about 1/1836 of the proton mass.

constants.name: Proton mass
constants.description: The rest mass of a proton, the nucleus of ordinary hydrogen.

constants.name: Neutron mass
constants.description: The rest mass of a neutron, slightly larger than the proton mass.

constants.name: Atomic mass constant
constants.description: One twelfth of the mass of a carbon-12 atom, also called the unified atomic mass unit (u) or dalton (Da).

constants.name: Vacuum electric permittivity
constants.description: Describes how easily an electric field forms in empty space. It appears in Coulomb's law and in the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor.

constants.name: Vacuum magnetic permeability
constants.description: Describes how easily a magnetic field forms in empty space. Very close to 4π × 10⁻⁷ N/A², but no longer exact since the 2019 SI revision.

constants.name: Coulomb constant
constants.description: Equal to 1/(4π ε₀). It sets the strength of the electric force between two charges in Coulomb's law.

constants.name: Fine-structure constant
constants.description: A pure number, about 1/137, that measures the strength of the electromagnetic interaction. It is the same in every system of units.

constants.name: Rydberg constant
constants.description: Sets the wavelengths of the spectral lines of hydrogen-like atoms (for an infinitely heavy nucleus). One of the most precisely measured constants.

constants.name: Bohr radius
constants.description: The radius of the smallest electron orbit in Bohr's model of hydrogen, a natural length scale for atoms.

constants.name: Bohr magneton
constants.description: The natural unit of the magnetic moment of an electron, equal to e ħ / (2 m_e).

constants.name: Nuclear magneton
constants.description: The natural unit of nuclear magnetic moments, equal to e ħ / (2 m_p). It is about 1836 times smaller than the Bohr magneton.

constants.name: Compton wavelength of the electron
constants.description: Equal to h / (m_e c). It is the wavelength shift of a photon scattered through 90 degrees by a free electron; the largest shift, for scattering straight back, is twice this.

constants.name: Classical electron radius
constants.description: The length at which the electrostatic energy of an electron would equal its rest energy. It sets the scale of Thomson scattering.

constants.name: Magnetic flux quantum
constants.description: Equal to h / (2e), the smallest unit of magnetic flux through a superconducting loop. Exact, shown to 10 significant figures.

constants.name: Characteristic impedance of vacuum
constants.description: Equal to μ₀ c, the ratio of electric to magnetic field strength in a light wave travelling through vacuum.

constants.name: Hartree energy
constants.description: The atomic unit of energy, twice the ionisation energy of hydrogen (about 27.2 eV). Used throughout quantum chemistry.

constants.name: Josephson constant
constants.description: Equal to 2e / h. Voltage standards use it: a Josephson junction driven at frequency f gives voltage steps of f / K_J.

constants.name: Von Klitzing constant
constants.description: Equal to h / e², the resistance quantum seen in the quantum Hall effect. Resistance standards are based on it.

constants.name: Caesium hyperfine transition frequency
constants.description: The frequency of the microwave transition in caesium-133 that defines the second. Atomic clocks count its cycles.

constants.name: Luminous efficacy of 540 THz radiation
constants.description: Converts the power of green light at 540 THz into how bright it looks to a human eye. It defines the candela.

constants.name: Standard atmosphere
constants.description: A reference air pressure close to the average at sea level. Used for standard temperature and pressure (STP) in older and chemistry conventions.

constants.name: Molar volume of an ideal gas at STP
constants.description: The volume of one mole of ideal gas at 273.15 K and 101.325 kPa, about 22.4 dm³. Equal to R T / p at those conditions.
constants.source: Derived from SI defining constants (CODATA 2018, 273.15 K and 101.325 kPa)

constants.name: Speed of sound in air at 20 °C
constants.description: A typical value for dry air at 20 °C and sea level pressure. It rises by about 0.6 m/s for every degree warmer.

constants.name: Density of water
constants.description: The rounded density of liquid water. More precisely it is 999.97 kg/m³ at 4 °C and 998.2 kg/m³ at 20 °C.

constants.name: Specific heat capacity of water
constants.description: The energy needed to warm 1 kg of liquid water by 1 K, at about 15 °C. School books often round it to 4180 or 4200.
constants.source: Typical value for liquid water near 15 °C

constants.name: Specific latent heat of fusion of water
constants.description: The energy needed to melt 1 kg of ice at 0 °C without changing its temperature.

constants.name: Specific latent heat of vaporisation of water
constants.description: The energy needed to turn 1 kg of water at 100 °C into steam at the same temperature.

constants.name: Ionic product of water at 25 °C
constants.description: The product of the hydrogen ion and hydroxide ion concentrations in water at 25 °C. It is temperature dependent and rises in warmer water.

constants.name: Mass of the Earth
constants.description: The total mass of the Earth, found from G M measured with satellites divided by G.
constants.source: IAU and NASA planetary fact sheet

constants.name: Mean radius of the Earth
constants.description: The mean radius of the Earth. The equator radius is about 6378 km and the pole radius about 6357 km.

constants.name: Mass of the Sun
constants.description: The mass of the Sun, about 333 000 Earth masses. Astronomers call it one solar mass.
constants.source: IAU (from the nominal solar mass parameter)

constants.name: Radius of the Sun
constants.description: The nominal radius of the Sun, about 109 Earth radii.

constants.name: Luminosity of the Sun
constants.description: The total power radiated by the Sun, used as the unit of luminosity for other stars.

constants.name: Solar constant
constants.description: The power of sunlight per square metre at the average Earth-Sun distance, measured above the atmosphere.

constants.name: Mass of the Moon
constants.description: The mass of the Moon, about 1/81 of the Earth's mass.

constants.name: Astronomical unit
constants.description: A length close to the average Earth-Sun distance, defined exactly by the IAU in 2012.

constants.name: Light-year
constants.description: The distance light travels in vacuum in one Julian year of 365.25 days.
constants.source: IAU (exact, c times one Julian year)

constants.name: Parsec
constants.description: The distance at which one astronomical unit spans an angle of one arcsecond, about 3.26 light-years.

constants.name: Pi
constants.description: The ratio of a circle's circumference to its diameter. Built into Calcy as pi.

constants.name: Euler's number
constants.description: The base of natural logarithms, the limit of (1 + 1/n)ⁿ as n grows. Built into Calcy as e.

constants.name: Golden ratio
constants.description: Equal to (1 + √5)/2. Two lengths are in the golden ratio when the whole is to the longer part as the longer part is to the shorter. Ratios of consecutive Fibonacci numbers approach it.

constants.name: Euler-Mascheroni constant
constants.description: The limit of 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + ... + 1/n minus ln(n) as n grows. It appears in number theory and analysis.

constants.name: Apéry's constant
constants.description: The sum 1 + 1/2³ + 1/3³ + 1/4³ + ..., the value of the Riemann zeta function at 3. Apéry proved it is irrational in 1978.
